title: Eastern Front
summary: The German-Soviet war ran from the invasion of 22 June 1941 to the surrender in May 1945 and was where the Second World War in Europe was decided: some thirty million of the war's dead, the great majority of German losses, and by most counts over four fifths of the fighting. It was also a war of extermination by design — the commissar order, the starvation of Soviet prisoners, the shooting of Jews behind the lines by the Einsatzgruppen — and not a campaign that became one. Its shape at the end, with the Red Army in Berlin and in every capital east of it, is the fact every post-war settlement in Europe had to start from.
